goal: Test only real event display + genuine refresh (new data appearing after a refresh, not a one-shot snapshot) through both Spike B and Spike C.

spike_b_selective_reuse.change: added refreshNonce state as the fetch effect's dependency, plus a 'Refresh' button (data-testid=refresh-button) that increments it, re-invoking the existing fetchLiveConversationAndEvents() call
spike_b_selective_reuse.lib/adapter/adapter-live-client.ts: unchanged - already exported reusable fetch functions

adapter_uncached_passthrough_confirmed.method: curl'd GET /api/conversations/:id/events/count against the running adapter-server immediately after each new event insertion, with no adapter restart between calls
adapter_uncached_passthrough_confirmed.conclusion: adapter-server/src/routes/events.ts calls latestExecutionEvents() fresh on every request with no caching layer - confirms the plan's 'no spike-c change needed' analysis

worker_lease_finding.requirement: request body's workerId must equal executions.lease_owner
worker_lease_finding.gap_found: seed.ts's own seed-output.json never recorded the random worker-<uuid> value used at claim time, and completing an execution does not clear lease_owner
worker_lease_finding.resolution: seed-followup-event.mjs does one read-only SELECT lease_owner FROM executions WHERE id=$1 before POSTing, same direct-Postgres-bypass pattern seed.ts already uses for its own setup

spike_c_refresh_mechanism.conclusion: no polling, no WebSocket, no focus/reconnect refetch under a statically-served build - refetchOnMount only fires on a genuine React mount, so a full browser page reload is the honest, verified refresh mechanism used for this side's test (not an assumption)

smoke_test_c.target: http://localhost:4173 (Spike A build, served via sirv) through Spike C's adapter at http://127.0.0.1:4100
known_preexisting_console_noise: WebSocket connection failures (404) to /sockets/bash-events and /sockets/events/:id - documented pre-existing limitation from Spikes A/C, not a regression
workspace-session CORS/credentials failure - pre-existing, unrelated to this spike's scope
